title: Cyclone Gezani (Toamasina, Madagascar) - Damage Assessment

resources.description:
Imagery coverage: 40 km² from March 29th as a follow up to the February 15th assessment. 

Results 

Out of a total of 78967 building footprints in the study area: 

5234 footprints were obscured by clouds 

Of the remaining 73733 non-cloudy footprints, the model predicted that 27266 (37.0%) were damaged to some extent2. 

We independently labeled 166 building footprints (each with area > 50 m²) from the source imagery. Of these, 146 footprints were uncloudy and could be reliably assessed as either “damaged” or “undamaged”. Using these samples, the model has an estimated recall of 83% and precision of 87%. Extrapolating this performance to all 30964 buildings with area > 50 m², we estimate: 13361 damaged buildings (43.2%) with a 95% confidence interval: [10871, 15851]. 

Between the two scenes there are 72,077 common building ids that are uncloudy. Of these: 

19,838 (27.5%) are undamaged in both 

5,271 (7.3%) were classified as undamaged originally, then damaged in this new scene (likely misclassifications) 

25,269 (32.1%) were damaged in original, then undamaged in this new scene 

21,699 (30.1%) are damaged in both

Imagery coverage: 90 km² from February 15th following the central track of the cyclone.  

Results 

Out of a total of 111,895 building footprints in the study area: 

23,076 footprints were obscured by clouds 

Of the remaining 88,819 non-cloudy footprints, the model predicted that 54,176 (60.9%) were damaged to some extent. 

We independently labeled 161 building footprints (each with area > 50 m²) from the source imagery. Of these, 138 footprints were uncloudy and could be reliably assessed as either “damaged” or “undamaged”. Using these samples, the model has an estimated recall of 97% and precision of 79%. Extrapolating this performance to all 41,188 buildings with area > 50 m², we estimate: 22,778 damaged buildings (55.3%) with a 95% confidence interval: [19,277, 26,279].
